name: Entity Framework Core
description: Entity Framework Core standard. Defines enforceable rules, implementation boundaries, failure handling and review evidence expected when STD-DOTNET-EF applies.

rules.title: Keep DbContext lifetime scoped to one unit of work
rules.detail: Do not share DbContext across threads or cache it beyond the application/request/job scope.
rules.example_good: The implementation and review evidence demonstrate: Keep DbContext lifetime scoped to one unit of work.
rules.example_bad: The change violates or ignores the rule: Keep DbContext lifetime scoped to one unit of work.

rules.title: Use explicit projections for read APIs
rules.detail: Select only required columns into response/read models; avoid loading large tracked entity graphs by default.
rules.example_good: The implementation and review evidence demonstrate: Use explicit projections for read APIs.
rules.example_bad: The change violates or ignores the rule: Use explicit projections for read APIs.

rules.title: Use AsNoTracking for read-only queries
rules.detail: Disable tracking when entities will not be updated to reduce memory and change-tracker overhead.
rules.example_good: The implementation and review evidence demonstrate: Use AsNoTracking for read-only queries.
rules.example_bad: The change violates or ignores the rule: Use AsNoTracking for read-only queries.

rules.title: Avoid N+1 query patterns
rules.detail: Inspect generated SQL and use projection/join/explicit loading appropriate to the use case rather than hidden per-row queries.
rules.example_good: The implementation and review evidence demonstrate: Avoid N+1 query patterns.
rules.example_bad: The change violates or ignores the rule: Avoid N+1 query patterns.

rules.title: Model concurrency and database constraints explicitly
rules.detail: Use concurrency tokens where needed and configure unique/foreign/check constraints that protect invariants.
rules.example_good: The implementation and review evidence demonstrate: Model concurrency and database constraints explicitly.
rules.example_bad: The change violates or ignores the rule: Model concurrency and database constraints explicitly.

rules.title: Apply migrations through controlled deployment
rules.detail: Do not auto-run unsafe production migrations on every app startup; review locking/backfill compatibility and use staged migration for breaking changes.
rules.example_good: The implementation and review evidence demonstrate: Apply migrations through controlled deployment.
rules.example_bad: The change violates or ignores the rule: Apply migrations through controlled deployment.

integration_guide.title: Resolve applicability and dependencies
integration_guide.description: Confirm where STD-DOTNET-EF applies and resolve its extends/implements/uses/aligns_with dependencies in the project standard profile.

integration_guide.title: Record project decisions
integration_guide.description: Apply the rules of Entity Framework Core to requirements/design/ADRs and record any project-specific thresholds, providers or justified exceptions.

integration_guide.title: Implement with evidence
integration_guide.description: Implement the applicable MUST/SHOULD rules and link code, configuration, tests or review evidence to the change.

integration_guide.title: Verify before completion
integration_guide.description: Run automated checks where possible and manual review for judgement-based rules; close or approve documented deviations.

common_issues.issue: Entity Framework Core is applied inconsistently across features
common_issues.cause: The project references the standard but does not resolve concrete ownership, thresholds or verification evidence.
common_issues.solution: Resolve dependencies, record project-specific decisions and include applicable rules in implementation/review checks.

common_issues.issue: Implementation satisfies the happy path but misses Entity Framework Core failure cases
common_issues.cause: Boundary, retry, security or recovery scenarios were not included in acceptance/test planning.
common_issues.solution: Use the standard rules to add explicit failure/recovery scenarios and verify them before release.
